title: 1 · Purpose and choice
text: Breathing Room is a local coursework prototype tested only with fictional scenarios. No required chat or questionnaire. The user chooses when to start, stop, or change display settings.

title: 2 · Explicit personalization
text: Display choices are saved in SQLite and remain changeable. We remember a chosen presentation; we do not infer distress from clicks or completed sessions.

title: 3 · Full exercise — real time
text: Six cycles: inhale for four counts, exhale for six. Application code controls the pacing, Pause and Stop. This recording keeps the full one-minute sequence at normal speed.

title: 4 · Completion and persistence
text: The completed session shows 60 active seconds and six cycles. Browser timing and SQLite/API comparisons are recorded separately in the evaluation evidence.

title: 5 · Useful saved history
text: History shows factual duration, outcome and display choice, with record IDs for verification. Activity counts do not establish emotional improvement.

title: 6 · Independent support and exit
text: Support information is bundled with the frontend. Opening it pauses the exercise. It works without a model response or classifier decision. No external service is contacted in this demo.

title: 7 · User control
text: Returning leaves the exercise paused. Resume requires an explicit choice. Stop remains available and records a neutral Stopped outcome.

title: 8 · Saved live-model contribution
text: This is an actual saved gpt-4.1-mini reply from the bounded live evaluation. The current server is in mock mode; replaying saved history makes no paid calls. AI labels stay attached to actual AI replies.

title: 9 · Refined model boundary
text: Repeated live testing exposed ambiguous pause-history claims. Because pause events are not recorded, this recognized question gets a fixed, accurately labeled app reply. Other wording can still escape the narrow rule.

title: 10 · Failure is visible
text: Browser test injection blocks API requests. The interface does not invent a saved reply. It retains the pending request for retry.

title: 11 · Support survives failure
text: The support panel still opens while API requests fail. This proves local access to the information; external services require their own connection.

title: 12 · Recovery and limits
text: Retry saves one exchange under the original request ID. The final report distinguishes mock, fixed and live evidence, records the model surprise, and lists untested limits. This prototype is not offered as a support service.
